successCriteria.description: A `LeavePolicyService` class exists in `src/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.service.ts` that satisfies the `ILeavePolicyService` interface declared in `./leave-policy.model.ts` — verified by TypeScript compilation (the class must compile without errors when assigned to a variable typed `ILeavePolicyService`).
The `LeavePolicyService` constructor accepts exactly one parameter of type `ILeavePolicyRepository` (the interface, not the concrete `PgLeavePolicyRepository`), satisfying dependency inversion.
`getPolicyForLeaveType(leaveType)` delegates to `this.repo.findByLeaveType(leaveType)` and returns its result directly — a `LeavePolicy | null`.

`validateEntitlement(employeeId, leaveType, requestedDays)` calls `this.repo.findByLeaveType(leaveType)`. If the repository returns `null` (no policy found), the method returns `false`. If a policy is found, the method returns `requestedDays <= policy.entitlementDays`.

constraints: The service must NOT access the database directly — all data access goes through the injected `ILeavePolicyRepository` (GP-001).
The service must NOT create audit records — both `getPolicyForLeaveType` and `validateEntitlement` are read-only operations (GP-002 applies only to state-changing operations).
The service must NOT import or reference `PgLeavePolicyRepository` — it depends only on the `ILeavePolicyRepository` interface from `./leave-policy.model.ts`.
outOfScope: Unit tests for `LeavePolicyService` — these are produced in sibling sub-phase 3/3.
The `PgLeavePolicyRepository` implementation — produced in sibling sub-phase 1/3.
The `PgEmployeeRepository` implementation — produced in sibling sub-phase 1/3.

entityInvariants.invariant: The service is stateless — it holds a reference to `ILeavePolicyRepository` but maintains no mutable state of its own. Every method call is a pure delegation or computation over repository results.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at this layer — the service is a pure business-logic component; auth is enforced at the controller/route layer.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no policy exists for the given leave type (not-found is not an error at this layer). Propagates any repository-level errors without wrapping.

interfaceConstraints.operation: validateEntitlement(employeeId: string, leaveType: LeaveType, requestedDays: number): Promise<boolean>
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth enforcement at this layer — the service is a pure business-logic component; auth is enforced at the controller/route layer.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns false when no policy exists for the leave type (graceful degradation — missing policy means no entitlement). Propagates any repository-level errors without wrapping. The employeeId parameter is accepted but not used in the lookup (entitlement is per leave type, not per employee).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `LeavePolicyService` class must satisfy the `ILeavePolicyService` interface exactly as declared in `./leave-policy.model.ts` — both method signatures (`getPolicyForLeaveType` and `validateEntitlement`) must match the interface's parameter types and return types.

The `LeaveType` parameter in both service methods must use the `LeaveType` enum imported from `../../shared/types`, matching the type used by `ILeavePolicyRepository.findByLeaveType` and the `LeavePolicy.leaveType` field.

integrationPoints.why: The service delegates all data access to the repository — `getPolicyForLeaveType` calls `findByLeaveType`, and `validateEntitlement` also calls `findByLeaveType`.
